name: No Resolving Neighbor after a Square Completion
statement: Let $G$ be nonempty, ample, and nonpeelable, and let $S=G\cup\{c\}$ be ample with acquired support $I$ of size at most two. No word adjacent to $c$ is a resolving one-concept addition to $S$. Consequently, the one-corner two-neighbor construction can have its required resolving neighbors only when $|I|\ge3$.
proof: For an adjacent ample addition $u=c^{\{f\}}$, one has $f\notin I$ and its acquired support over $S$ is $P=J\cup\{f\}$ for some $J\subseteq I$. Rank-two extension invariance keeps $S$ nonpeelable and excludes resolution when $|J|\le1$. The only remaining case has $I=J$ of size two. Removing $c$ leaves the punctured $I$-square at $u$ and removes only its $f$-neighbor, so $G\cup\{u\}$ is ample and also acquires $I$. Square-pair invariance then makes $S\cup\{u\}$ nonpeelable.
comments: The fixed controls certify nonpeelability before and after square completion at orders 293 and 294, and after one and two adjacent completions in a punctured-square product at orders 874 and 875.
